# Deep Residual Learning

Residual connections make very deep networks trainable: the layer learns a correction to
the identity instead of the whole mapping.

- The paper compares plain and residual nets of 18, 34, 50, 101 and 152 layers on ImageNet.
- A 34-layer plain net has *higher* training error than an 18-layer one; the residual version
  fixes that, so the problem was optimization, not capacity.
- Bottleneck blocks keep depth affordable: 1x1, 3x3, 1x1 convolutions.

Useful for the encoder of anything that reads sensor traces: depth no longer costs accuracy.
